display.purpose: Section statements and the name. Sentence case, always with a full stop.

condensed.purpose: Role lines, poster titles inside sheets, pull quotes.

label.purpose: Stamps, sheet headers, metadata, legend. Never below 8.5px.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: Every pasted sheet. Follows the torn contour instead of a rounded box.

shadows.name: slip-contact
shadows.purpose: Small chalk slips and nav tabs: tight contact shadow only.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Hero overprint sliding from 9px to 5px off-register, once, then still.

motion.name: paper
motion.purpose: Sticker snap, button lift, link rule thickening.

motion.name: fold
motion.purpose: Project sheet corner lift and panel reveal.

motion.name: menu
motion.purpose: Mobile menu fade only; the board itself does not slide.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Chalk slip on red or board. Square, condensed uppercase, lifts 2px on hover.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Outlined on red or blue. Inverts to chalk fill on hover.

components.name: Nav Tab
components.description: A pasted tab with its own rotation. The current section snaps straight and turns red.
components.html: TravauxStack

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: A stamped 1px rectangle, slightly rotated. Never a pill, never filled.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; background: transparent; color: #b02e20; border: 1px solid #b02e20; border-radius: 0; padding: 4px 6px; font-family: 'Courier Prime', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 8.5px; line-height: 1.4; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.12em; transform: rotate(-2deg); }

narrative.overview:
A hoarding on a Douala street: posters pasted over older posters, edges torn back by hand, tape still on them. Nothing is framed; everything is stuck to a wall of warm grey board, with chalk paper, near-black ink and two printing inks — red and deep blue.

Depth means history, not elevation. A newer sheet sits on top of an older one and hides part of it, so the reader feels the earlier versions underneath. That is the argument of the page: a career is layered, and the person you hire is the top sheet.

The voice is first person and short. Facts sit in Courier Prime like a stamped record, statements in Archivo Black like a headline pasted up by hand, and reading text stays quiet in Public Sans so the posters can be loud.
keyCharacteristics: Pasted sheets with hand-torn bottom edges, never rounded cards
Four typefaces in fixed roles: display, condensed facts, stamped labels, reading text
Flat colour fields that change abruptly at a torn seam
Red and blue used as poster ink, not as UI accent
Motion only where paper would move

rules.name: The Ink-On-Board Rule
rules.body: Red and blue never carry small text on board. On board, small text is ink or ink-faint; red is a rule, a stamp border, or a fill large enough to hold chalk.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Red and blue never share a field. A section is board, chalk, red, blue or ink — one ground, one ink.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: A heading is a statement, not a category. No eyebrow or kicker above a heading; the label sits under the thing it names.

dos: Do tear the bottom edge of a sheet and leave the top edge straight.
Do put small text on board in ink or ink-faint, and reserve red for fills, rules and stamps.
Do keep technical terms in English in both languages.
Do let one sheet overlap the next, and pad the sheet underneath so no label is covered.
Do keep the tear deterministic with a fixed seed per sheet.
donts: Don't round a corner, add a pill, or nest a card inside a sheet.
Don't put a kicker above a heading, number a section, or add a divider rule between fields.
Don't use red or blue small text on board, and don't put ink text on red.
Don't animate section entrances; motion belongs to paper only.
Don't use gradient text, coloured border-left callouts, hard offset shadows, or glows.
Don't invent a metric, a percentage, a duration or a logo to fill space.
